statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain no derivation of the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), defining it directly as the nonlinear extension of the Kalman filter that linearizes about an estimate of the current mean and covariance. For a continuous-time system with discrete-time measurements given by $\dot{\mathbf{x}}(t) = f(\mathbf{x}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)) + \mathbf{w}(t)$ with $\mathbf{w}(t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{Q}(t))$ and discrete measurements $\mathbf{z}_k = h(\mathbf{x}_k) + \mathbf{v}_k$ with $\mathbf{v}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{R}_k)$ at times $t_k$, the first-order EKF is defined by: (1) Initialization: $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{0|0} = \mathbb{E}[\mathbf{x}(t_0)]$, $\mathbf{P}_{0|0} = \mathbb{E}[(\mathbf{x}(t_0) - \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_0))(\mathbf{x}(t_0) - \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_0))^T]$; (2) Prediction: solve $\dot{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}(t) = f(\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t))$ and $\dot{\mathbf{P}}(t) = \mathbf{F}(t)\mathbf{P}(t) + \mathbf{P}(t)\mathbf{F}(t)^T + \mathbf{Q}(t)$ from $t_{k-1}$ to $t_k$ with initial conditions $\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_{k-1}) = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k-1|k-1}$ and $\mathbf{P}(t_{k-1}) = \mathbf{P}_{k-1|k-1}$, yielding $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}(t_k)$ and $\mathbf{P}_{k|k-1} = \mathbf{P}(t_k)$, where $\mathbf{F}(t) = \left.\frac{\partial f}{\partial \mathbf{x}}\right|_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)}$; and (3) Update: $\mathbf{K}_k = \mathbf{P}_{k|k-1}\mathbf{H}_k^T(\mathbf{H}_k\mathbf{P}_{k|k-1}\mathbf{H}_k^T + \mathbf{R}_k)^{-1}$, $\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k} = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1} + \mathbf{K}_k(\mathbf{z}_k - h(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1}))$, and $\mathbf{P}_{k|k} = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_k\mathbf{H}_k)\mathbf{P}_{k|k-1}$, where $\mathbf{H}_k = \left.\frac{\partial h}{\partial \mathbf{x}}\right|_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}_{k|k-1}}$.

properties.property: In the continuous-time extended Kalman filter, prediction and update steps are coupled into a continuous differential equation
properties.why: The state estimate differential equation includes the innovation term simultaneously with system dynamics

properties.property: The measurement update equations for continuous-time models with discrete-time measurements are identical to those of the discrete-time extended Kalman filter
properties.why: Discrete measurements update state and covariance algebraically at discrete measurement times

properties.property: The standard EKF recursion is a first-order filter that can be extended to higher-order filters
properties.why: Linearization retains only the first-order terms of Taylor series expansions of f and h

properties.property: Higher-order extended Kalman filters tend to only provide performance benefits when measurement noise is small
properties.why: Higher-order Taylor series retention only provides performance advantages under small measurement noise conditions

properties.property: The extended Kalman filter formulation accommodates non-additive process and measurement noise
properties.why: General systems can incorporate noise parameters directly inside nonlinear transition and measurement mappings

assumptions.assumption: Process noise w(t) and measurement noise v_k are zero-mean Gaussian distributed with covariances Q(t) and R_k, respectively
assumptions.breaks_when: Disturbances exhibit heavy-tailed, multimodal, or biased non-Gaussian distributions

assumptions.assumption: The nonlinear functions f and h are sufficiently well approximated by their first-order Taylor series expansions evaluated at the state estimate
assumptions.breaks_when: The system dynamics or measurement functions are severely nonlinear across the uncertainty region of the state

assumptions.assumption: The innovation covariance matrix (H_k P_{k|k-1} H_k^T + R_k) is positive-definite and invertible
assumptions.breaks_when: Measurement noise covariance R_k is singular and measurement projections are linearly dependent

assumptions.assumption: Process noise and measurement noise enter additively in the standard continuous-discrete formulation
assumptions.breaks_when: Physical noise enters nonlinearly through state dynamics or sensor equations

failure_modes.mode: Filter divergence due to severe nonlinearity
failure_modes.signature: State estimation errors grow without bound while estimated covariance P remains optimistically small
failure_modes.cause: First-order Taylor series Jacobians F and H fail to accurately represent dynamics far from the expansion point

failure_modes.mode: Performance degradation in higher-order EKFs under large noise
failure_modes.signature: Higher-order EKF achieves worse estimation accuracy than a first-order EKF
failure_modes.cause: Higher-order Taylor series expansion terms provide performance benefits only when measurement noise is small

failure_modes.signature: Covariance matrix P develops negative eigenvalues or inversion of innovation covariance fails
failure_modes.cause: Finite-precision round-off errors in the algebraic covariance update (I - K_k H_k) P_{k|k-1} or ill-conditioned R_k

instantiation.why_here: In agrios_ws, the Extended Kalman Filter is used by the robot_localization nodes ekf_local and ekf_global to estimate the robot's pose and velocity. It fuses continuous motion model predictions with discrete sensor observations from odometry and IMU sources to maintain filtered state and covariance estimates. The algorithm handles system non-linearities by linearizing state and measurement transitions around current estimates while accounting for process and sensor noise.

concrete.in_your_project: The updated robot state estimate vector [n x 1] computed at step k for base_link_frame base_footprint.
The state error covariance matrix [n x n] representing estimate uncertainty, initialized via initial_estimate_covariance.
The process noise covariance matrix [n x n] set by process_noise_covariance, modeling uncertainty in vehicle motion dynamics.
Discrete measurement vectors [m x 1] received at step k from sensor inputs such as /imu (imu0, imu1) and odometry sources (odom0, odom1).
The measurement Jacobian matrix [m x n] selecting which components of the state vector are observed, configured via sensor boolean masks.
The measurement noise covariance matrix [m x m] corresponding to sensor noise from active odometry and IMU measurement streams.
The Kalman gain matrix [n x m] computed at step k to weight sensor innovation against prediction covariance during the update step.
